messages:
incident-bot: Pager: routing.fallback.high_error_rate in prod (severity=page). Auto-detected spike in fallback events + retry amplification. Paging Priya (oncall).

Priya (oncall): On it. Root TS 1815001234. What's the impact? Are customers seeing 5xxs or just higher latency? :pager:

Tom K.: Seeing both. Errors jump from 0.2% to ~12% in last 2m. Latency p95 doubled. Core metric: fallback_count -> up 18x. QPS routing to fallback targets doubled. Suspect cascade from retry behavior.

Zoe (infra): Dumping quick logs and metrics. Here's the error tail:
```
2026-03-15T10:23:10Z service=inference region=us-east-1 target=variant-v2 status=200
2026-03-15T10:23:11Z service=inference region=us-east-1 target=variant-v1 status=503 error=kv-cache-miss
2026-03-15T10:23:12Z service=inference region=us-west-2 target=variant-xxl status=200 fallback=true
2026-03-15T10:23:12Z retry=client attempts=1
2026-03-15T10:23:13Z retry=client attempts=2
2026-03-15T10:23:13Z service=inference region=us-west-2 target=variant-xxl status=504
```
Pattern: clients retry immediately -> routing policy sends to a heavier variant in another region as fallback -> heavier variant slower -> clients retry again -> more fallbacks. Amplification loop.

Priya (oncall): Got it. Is this a routing policy misconfig (wrong fallback variant) or a region failover loop? Which policy fired?

Zoe (infra): Policy that fired: smart-routing policy 'regional-fallback-v1' has a fallback mapping that was recently changed in the rollout. Instead of fallback -> variant-lite in same region, it now points to variant-xxl in us-west-2 for certain model families. That was the bad change.

Tom K.: Also noticed client SDKs send up to 3 immediate retries (no backoff) on http 5xx for streaming endpoints. So each failed request spawns multiple extra requests within 100-200ms. Combined that's the amplifier.

Priya (oncall): Immediate plan: 1) Stop the fallback to variant-xxl, 2) Add temporary rate-limit on fallback path, 3) ask SRE to scale serving pool for the targeted variant if needed. Who can flip the policy quickly?

Zoe (infra): I can flip the routing mapping to point back to variant-lite in-region. Command I will run:
```
# WARNING: runs in control-plane
redwoodctl routing set-mapping --policy regional-fallback-v1 --model-family family-abc --fallback variant-lite --region us-east-1
```
I'll run that now and watch.

Luis (sre): While Zoe does that, I'll add a short-term rate limit on fallback routes and throttle client retries at the gateway edge.
```
# rate limit fallback path
redwoodctl quota set --path /v1/generate?fallback=true --qps 50
# edge config to enforce exponential backoff on retry header
edgectl set retry-policy --default-backoff 200ms --max-attempts 2
```

Priya (oncall): Thanks. Anna from CS, can you surface to customers who reported errors? We might need to update status page.

Anna (cs): On it — will message the impacted accounts and put a note on status.redwood.ai: brief outage impacting some gen API calls, mitigation in progress. Will link to this thread.

Zoe (infra): Mapping flipped. Observability: fallback_count started dropping within 30s. Errors down from 12% -> 3% and latency p95 trending down. Keep watching for retry echoes.

Tom K.: Confirmed: QPS to us-west-2 variant-xxl dropped 85%. Client retry attempts also decreased as upstream calls started succeeding. No additional downstream spikes.

Priya (oncall): Great. Root cause summary (draft): incorrect rollout of regional-fallback-v1 mapping pointed some model families to heavyweight cross-region variant-xxl. Client SDKs with aggressive immediate retry settings amplified failures into a traffic cascade (retry amplification). This combination created a transient thundering-fallback that increased 5xxs and latency. Action items:
- Zoe: revert mapping + validate rollout pipeline to prevent bad mapping (in progress)
- Luis: add short-term edge retry guardrails and a fallback rate-limit (done)
- Tom: audit client SDK retry defaults and add exponential jitter (follow-up)
- Anna: customer comms and status update (in progress)
- Priya: create incident and assign Sev2 postmortem, include test prompts for regen tests

Luis (sre): Will follow up with a new edge rule: any path flagged fallback=true will be limited and include an opt-in header before heavy variants.

Zoe (infra): Also adding an automated rollback guard to our rollout pipeline: if fallback_count jumps >5x within 2m of change, auto-revert and notify owners.

Priya (oncall): Sounds good. Leaving on-call notes here and handing back to regular rotation at 11:00. Thanks all. I'll open the incident ticket and add the timeline + raw logs.

incident-bot: Incident created: INC-2026-0348. Severity: S2. Link: https://internal.redwood/INC-2026-0348

Anna (cs): Status update posted to status.redwood.ai. Messaging to impacted customers scheduled.

Tom K.: Follow-ups: I'll prep a small internal doc on safe fallback mappings and recommended client retry policy. Suggest default SDK change: exponential backoff with base 200ms + jitter, max attempts 2 for streaming endpoints.

Priya (oncall): Final note: if anyone sees a re-spike, @Priya (oncall) and @Luis (sre) are the fast responders. Postmortem owner: Tom K. ETA for draft: EOD tomorrow.

Zoe (infra): Thanks everyone. Closing the page. :white_check_mark:
